facts: Healing is a process by which the body repairs damaged tissue.
Cells work together to fix injuries over time.
Sometimes damaged tissue is replaced with healthy tissue of the same kind.
Sometimes damaged tissue is replaced with scar tissue instead.
false_claims: Healing means damaged tissue never changes.
notes: Reviewed: split colon-style bullet into two scorable facts.

facts: The International English Language Testing System (IELTS) measures English fluency.
Test takers choose the Academic Module or the General Training Module.
The Academic Module is for people applying to university.
The General Training Module is for work, training, or immigration.
notes: Reviewed: domain=other; consolidated redundant module facts.

facts: Ink is a liquid that is used to write, draw, print, or make marks.
Ink is used in pens, in some computer printers, and in printing presses.
In some countries, people write by using ink and brushes.
People usually write or print using black ink, but ink can be any color.
The first ink was used in Egypt about 2600 BC.
false_claims: Ink is a solid metal used only in factories.
notes: Reviewed: added rater trap; facts unchanged.

facts: The inch is a unit of length in the Imperial and U.S. customary systems.
Inches are written as in or with the double-prime symbol.
There are 12 inches in one foot.
One inch equals 2.54 centimeters.
notes: Reviewed: clarified abbreviation wording after broken extraction.

facts: An insult is words that offend or hurt someone.
An insult may or may not be true.
Insults are a form of derogatory language.
Words like foolish or stupid insult a person's intelligence.
false_claims: An insult is always a true statement of fact.
